defects.description: Across the enlarged and native proofs, the bicycle is visibly undersized relative to the bicycle anchors. Heavy strokes within the smaller footprint tighten the wheel openings and crowd the 1× rendering.
defects.treatment: Increase the bicycle’s optical size toward the bicycle anchors while preserving family stroke weight and clear wheel openings.

defects.description: The filled proof repeats the smaller bicycle footprint and cramped wheel openings. The resulting density is visible at 1× in both paint polarities compared with the bicycle anchors.
defects.treatment: Match the bicycle anchors’ optical scale and open the wheel counters, then recheck both paint polarities at native size.

defects.description: The bicycle is visibly smaller than both bicycle anchors while retaining heavy strokes, crowding the wheel counters. At native 16px/1x, the wheel openings lose the anchors’ clearer separation around the frame and fork. The issue appears in both polarities.
defects.treatment: Enlarge the bicycle and wheel counters toward the bicycle anchors’ proportions, then recheck native legibility in both polarities.

defects.description: The filled proof shows the same reduced bicycle footprint and cramped wheel counters. Enlarged geometry remains recognizable, but the 16px/1x wheel interiors are visibly less open than the bicycle anchors in both polarities.
defects.treatment: Increase the wheel openings and overall bicycle scale while preserving family stroke weight; verify at 1x and 2x.

comparison.mechanismFinding: A157 exercised one compiler repair and one visual repair under separate counters. The first inspected A157 proofs exactly equal the retained A156 proofs; the second inspection has no named defects and became the delivered result.

before: Both paints were undersized relative to bicycle anchors.
Heavy strokes in the smaller footprint crowded wheel counters at native 16px.
namedDefectTransition.after: A157 self reinspection reported no visible defects after enlarging the bicycle and opening wheel counters.
namedDefectTransition.boundary: This establishes lifecycle execution and removal of the author self-inspection finding. It does not establish independent craft quality.

nativeFootprint.pixelObservation: At native 16px on the light-background PNG, the thresholded foreground bbox changed from 14x10 at x=1,y=3 for both A156 paints to 16x12 at x=0,y=2 for both A157 paints. Foreground counts changed from 97/95 to 125/125 outlined/filled.

comparison.conclusion: The repair mechanism converted the rejected undersized A156 geometry into exact copies of the exposed same-paint mountain-bike proof anchors. Count this only as exposed-source reconstruction and a successful compile-to-inspect-to-visual-repair mechanism trace, never as novel generation or visual qualification.

preservedDefects.detail: The frozen manifest launch descriptor names A156 and overstates concurrency. Actual A157 dispatch was bound separately; this receipt does not repair the descriptor.
A157 has no qualified critic consensus. A complete single Codex development review remains insufficient for qualification.

limitations: Pixel footprint uses a stated deterministic color-difference threshold; it is evidence of occupied raster extent, not a visual-quality score.
Author self-inspection defect removal is not independent review.
Exact anchor-byte reproduction makes this case unsuitable as evidence of novel-family generation.

independentReview.finding: Both reviews completed and found no critical defect, but scores were 9 and 8. This does not meet a craft median >=9 gate and cannot qualify an exact exposed-anchor reconstruction as novel generation.
